title: Responsible AI begins before the model
excerpt: A practical framework for deciding whether an AI system should exist, what it should optimize, and who gets to question it.

sections.label: Premise
sections.title: The first design decision is whether to build.
paragraphs: Responsible development does not start at model selection. It starts with the people affected, the existing process, and an honest account of what automation might erase as well as improve.

sections.label: Framework
sections.title: Four questions before a prototype.
points: Who experiences the benefit, and who absorbs the risk?
Can a simpler rule or interface solve the problem?
What evidence would cause us to stop?
Can an affected person understand and contest the output?

sections.label: Practice
sections.title: Treat limits as product features.
paragraphs: Uncertainty, provenance, correction, and refusal should be designed into the main experience. They are not disclaimers to add after a demo succeeds.
